rules.title: Security Policy Documentation
rules.description_short: Repository must have a SECURITY.md file for reporting security vulnerabilities.
rules.description_long: Your repository should have a SECURITY.md file (or equivalent) that explains how users can report security vulnerabilities. This demonstrates commitment to coordinated vulnerability disclosure, which CRA requires.

rules.title: Dependency Inventory (SBOM)
rules.description_short: Maintain an inventory of all dependencies for transparency in your product.
rules.description_long: You must maintain an inventory of all dependencies (Software Bill of Materials). CRA requires transparency about what components are in your product. Lockfiles and manifest files serve as a basic SBOM.

rules.title: Dependency Vulnerability Management
rules.description_short: Manage known vulnerabilities in dependencies to mitigate compliance risks.
rules.description_long: You must actively manage known vulnerabilities in dependencies. CRA requires that products address security issues promptly. Having vulnerable dependencies is a compliance risk.

rules.title: Secure Default Configuration
rules.description_short: Products should be secure-by-default with no unnecessary attack surface.
rules.description_long: Products should be secure-by-default. Default settings should not expose unnecessary attack surface. This includes: no default passwords, secure connection settings enabled by default, minimal permissions, etc.

rules.title: Update and Patch Management
rules.description_short: Process for providing security updates and patches to address vulnerabilities.
rules.description_long: CRA requires that products can be updated to address vulnerabilities. Evidence includes: release tags, changelog, update documentation.

references.note: Compliance with update and patch management requirements.

rules.title: Security Testing in CI/CD
rules.description_short: Automated security testing must be part of the CI/CD process to ensure proactive security validation.
rules.description_long: You should have automated security testing as part of your build/deployment process. This demonstrates proactive security validation, which CRA expects.

rules.title: Documentation of Security Features
rules.description_short: Products must provide adequate documentation for security-relevant features.
rules.description_long: Users must understand how to use your product securely. CRA requires that products provide adequate documentation. Security-relevant features should be documented.

rules.title: No Hardcoded Secrets
rules.description_short: Secrets must never be committed to version control to avoid security risks.
rules.description_long: Secrets (API keys, passwords, tokens) must never be committed to version control. This is a fundamental security requirement and CRA violation risk. Applies to all repositories, especially those with CI/CD configurations where secrets often leak.

rules.title: Dependency Pinning and Reproducibility
rules.description_short: Dependencies must be pinned to specific versions to ensure reproducible builds.
rules.description_long: Dependencies should be pinned to specific versions (not '^1.0.0' or 'latest'). This ensures reproducible builds and prevents unexpected updates that could introduce vulnerabilities.

rules.title: Container Security (Dockerfile Best Practices)
rules.description_short: Containers must follow security best practices including non-root users and minimal base images.
rules.description_long: If you use containers (Docker), they should follow security best practices: non-root user, minimal base images, no secrets, health checks, etc. This demonstrates secure-by-design principles.

rules.title: Lifecycle Management Evidence
rules.description_short: Demonstrate active maintenance and lifecycle plan for your product.
rules.description_long: You must demonstrate that your product is actively maintained and has a lifecycle plan. CRA requires products to be supported throughout their lifecycle. Evidence includes: recent commits, maintenance status, deprecation notices if applicable.

rules.title: Access Control Documentation
rules.description_short: Documentation of authentication and authorization features is required for secure access control configuration.
rules.description_long: If your product has authentication/authorization features, they must be documented. Users need to understand how to configure access controls securely. CRA requires adequate documentation of security features.

rules.title: Encryption and Data Protection
rules.description_short: Sensitive data must be encrypted and documented to ensure data protection.
rules.description_long: If your product handles sensitive data, encryption should be used and documented. CRA requires appropriate security measures for data protection. Evidence includes: encryption configuration, TLS/SSL settings, data protection documentation.

rules.title: Incident Response Preparation
rules.description_short: Documentation on handling security incidents is required for preparedness.
rules.description_long: You should have documentation about how security incidents are handled. While CRA's incident reporting is primarily organizational, having documentation in the repo shows preparedness.

rules.title: Build and Deployment Security
rules.description_short: Ensure secure build and deployment processes throughout the product lifecycle.
rules.description_long: Your build and deployment process should be secure. This includes secure CI/CD configuration, signed artifacts, and secure deployment procedures. CRA expects security throughout the product lifecycle.

rules.title: Third-Party Component Assessment
rules.description_short: Assess third-party components for security and compliance.
rules.description_long: You should assess third-party components (dependencies) for security and compliance. CRA requires knowing what's in your product. Having a process for dependency assessment demonstrates due diligence.

rules.title: Version and Release Management
rules.description_short: Identify product versions and changes to support vulnerability management.
rules.description_long: You must be able to identify which version of your product is deployed and what changes are in each version. This supports vulnerability management and update processes required by CRA.

references.article: CRA Article 11 - Version identification for updates

rules.title: Secure Communication Documentation
rules.description_short: Secure communication (TLS/HTTPS) must be required and documented for networked products.
rules.description_long: If your product communicates over networks, secure communication (TLS/HTTPS) should be required and documented. CRA requires secure-by-design, which includes secure network communication.

REM-001.description:
Create Security Policy Document
- Action: Create SECURITY.md file in repository root or .github/ directory
- Template: Include contact email, response time commitment, scope of
  vulnerabilities to report
- Verification: File exists and contains security contact information
- Timeline: Can be done immediately (1 hour)

REM-002.description:
Implement Dependency Lockfiles
- Action: Generate and commit dependency lockfiles (package-lock.json,
  Pipfile.lock, etc.)
- Tools: npm install, pipenv lock, poetry lock
- Verification: Lockfile exists and is committed to version control
- Timeline: Immediate for existing projects, ongoing for new dependencies

REM-003.description:
Set Up Dependency Vulnerability Scanning
- Action: Integrate vulnerability scanning into development workflow
- Tools: npm audit, pip-audit, Snyk, Dependabot, OWASP Dependency-Check
- Verification: Scanning runs automatically (CI/CD or pre-commit)
- Timeline: 1-2 days for setup, ongoing monitoring

REM-004.description:
Remove Hardcoded Secrets
- Action: Audit codebase for secrets, remove them, rotate exposed secrets
- Tools: git-secrets, truffleHog, gitleaks, GitGuardian
- Verification: No secrets detected in scans, .env in .gitignore
- Timeline: Immediate (rotate secrets), 1 day for cleanup

REM-005.description:
Implement Secure Defaults
- Action: Review and update default configurations to be secure
- Steps: Remove default passwords, use environment variables, add .env.example
- Verification: No secrets in config files, secure defaults documented
- Timeline: 1-2 days depending on config complexity

REM-006.description:
Add Security Testing to CI/CD
- Action: Add security scanning steps to CI/CD pipeline
- Tools: CodeQL, Semgrep, Bandit, Snyk, OWASP ZAP
- Verification: Security tests run on every PR/commit
- Timeline: 2-3 days for initial setup

REM-007.description:
Create Security Documentation
- Action: Add security section to README and/or create dedicated security docs
- Content: Security features, secure configuration, vulnerability reporting
- Verification: Documentation exists and is accessible
- Timeline: 1 day for initial documentation

REM-008.description:
Implement Dependency Pinning
- Action: Pin all dependencies to exact versions, commit lockfiles
- Tools: Update manifest files, generate lockfiles
- Verification: No version ranges in manifests, lockfiles committed
- Timeline: 1 day for existing projects

REM-009.description:
Secure Dockerfile Configuration
- Action: Update Dockerfile to use non-root user, minimal base image
- Steps: Add USER directive, switch to alpine/distroless base, add HEALTHCHECK
- Verification: Dockerfile follows security best practices
- Timeline: 1 day

REM-010.description:
Document Update and Patch Process
- Action: Create CHANGELOG.md and document update procedures
- Content: How to update, version history, update notifications
- Verification: CHANGELOG exists, update process documented
- Timeline: 1 day

REM-011.description:
Establish Lifecycle Management
- Action: Document maintenance status and lifecycle policy
- Content: Support duration, maintenance schedule, EOL policy
- Verification: Lifecycle information in README or docs
- Timeline: 1 day

REM-012.description:
Document Access Controls
- Action: Create authentication/authorization documentation
- Content: How auth works, how to configure, security considerations
- Verification: Auth documentation exists
- Timeline: 1-2 days depending on complexity

REM-013.description:
Document Encryption Approach
- Action: Document how encryption is used in the product
- Content: Encryption at rest, in transit, key management
- Verification: Encryption documentation exists
- Timeline: 1 day

REM-014.description:
Create Incident Response Documentation
- Action: Add incident response section to SECURITY.md
- Content: How to report, response timeline, contact information
- Verification: Incident response info in SECURITY.md
- Timeline: 1 day

REM-015.description:
Secure Build and Deployment
- Action: Review and secure CI/CD configuration
- Steps: Use secrets management, add security checks, document process
- Verification: CI/CD uses secrets, no hardcoded credentials
- Timeline: 2-3 days

REM-016.description:
Establish Dependency Assessment Process
- Action: Document dependency selection and approval process
- Content: Assessment criteria, approval workflow
- Verification: Dependency policy document exists
- Timeline: 1 day

REM-017.description:
Implement Version Management
- Action: Add version tracking and use semantic versioning
- Steps: Add version to code, use git tags, create CHANGELOG
- Verification: Version is trackable, releases are tagged
- Timeline: 1 day

REM-018.description:
Document Secure Communication Requirements
- Action: Document TLS/HTTPS requirements
- Content: TLS version requirements, certificate management
- Verification: Secure communication documented
- Timeline: 1 day
